name: EGYPT

flag.title: Flag of Egypt
flag.note: Red, white & black; golden Eagle of Saladin

lead: Egypt sits at the crossroads of Africa and Asia, where the Nile turns desert into farmland. Pyramids built 4,500 years ago still stand as tall as a 48-storey building. More than 107 million people live here, making it the most populous Arab country on Earth — a place where ancient wonders and busy modern cities share the same horizon.
geo: Egypt is 96% desert — the Sahara and Eastern Desert leave only a narrow green ribbon along the Nile. That ribbon is just 5% of the land yet holds almost everyone. The Nile flows 6,650 km north before fanning into the Mediterranean through a vast fertile Delta.

The Sinai Peninsula juts into the Red Sea like a triangle, connecting Africa to Asia. Its coral reefs are world-class. The Suez Canal slices through the northeast, letting ships sail between seas — saving weeks of ocean travel around Africa.
animals: The Nile crocodile can reach 6 metres and was once worshipped as the god Sobek. Today they survive in Lake Nasser behind the Aswan High Dam. Sacred ibis — with curved black beaks — were mummified by the millions as offerings to Thoth, the god of wisdom.

The fennec fox roams the Western Desert on enormous ears that dump body heat on cool desert nights. Scarab beetles roll dung into perfect balls and became ancient Egypt's symbol of rebirth. Dugongs graze quietly on Red Sea seagrass far from the crowds.
culture: Egyptians are famously warm hosts — refusing a second helping is nearly unthinkable. Ful medames (slow-cooked fava beans) and koshari (lentils, rice, pasta, tangy tomato sauce) are eaten every day, loved equally by schoolchildren and presidents.

During Ramadan, streets fill with glowing lanterns called fanous and families break fast together at iftar. Arabic calligraphy — looping, flowing script — decorates mosques, wedding cards, and tattoos alike, treasured across the Arab world as the highest art form.
history: Egypt's first pharaoh united the country around 3100 BCE — over 5,100 years ago. For 3,000 years pharaohs ruled a civilisation that invented writing, the 365-day calendar, and advanced surgery. The Great Pyramid was Earth's tallest structure for nearly 4,000 years.

Greek, Roman, Arab, Ottoman, and British rulers each left their mark before independence in 1952. The Arab conquest in 641 CE brought Islam and Arabic. In 1869 the Suez Canal opened, making Egypt one of the world's most strategically vital countries overnight.
wows: The Great Pyramid holds enough stone to build a wall around France.
Ancient Egyptians invented the 365-day calendar over 5,000 years ago.
Cairo's metro is Africa's oldest subway, carrying over 3.5 million riders a day.
More ancient obelisks stand in Rome than in all of Egypt.
The Nile Delta was built entirely from mud carried from the Ethiopian Highlands.
Tutankhamun became pharaoh at just nine years old.
Egypt grows over 2 million tonnes of dates every year — more than any other country.

myths.fact: Evidence shows well-fed, paid workers and skilled craftsmen built the pyramids, living in purpose-built villages with medical care — not enslaved people.
Egypt has lush Nile farmland, Mediterranean beaches, world-class Red Sea reefs, and Cairo — a city of 20 million bursting with food, music, and history.
